mechanisms: Visible consumption signals unobserved wealth relative to a reference group, so the urge to set oneself apart intensifies when intra-group inequality is high and mean income is low.

Asset accumulation anchors new middle-class entrants, reducing vulnerability and the need to signal — conversely, conspicuous consumption is heightened precisely while status remains new or tenuous, before assets have accumulated enough to stabilize it.

Black Tax is a social and moral obligation rooted in African communalism, so financial products are evaluated by their capacity to help manage extended-family duties without undermining personal financial health.

Affordability, convenience, and accessibility are paramount for the income-insecure, so mobile-phone-based services that are trusted via word-of-mouth are adopted while formal products requiring payslips or collateral are avoided.
objection_patterns: Does this product visibly signal my middle-class status to my reference group?
Will this product help me accumulate assets that anchor my position in the middle class?
Can I use this product to budget for my extended-family obligations without sacrificing my own financial health?
Is this product affordable, accessible via my mobile phone, and trusted by people in my social network?
confidence: multi-source synthesis combining quantitative survey analysis, qualitative media framing analysis, and ethnographic fieldwork; mechanisms are robust across contexts but magnitudes are unknown.
